blocks.title: Introduction
blocks.content: Categorification of link invariants has been a fruitful program that has deepened and broadened our understanding of link invariants. Beginning with the advent of the Khovanov homology that categorifies the (colored) Jones polynomials of links [@Kh]([@Kh2]), there has been a series of constructions of other link invariants such as categorification of $sl(N)$ polynomial by $sl(N)$ Khovanov-Rozannsky homology [@KR] and the HOMFLY homology [@KR2] that categorifies the HOMFLY polynomial. blocks.content: In [@GPPV], it was conjectured that the $sl(2)$ WRT invariant of a rational homology 3-sphere $Y\, (b_1(Y)=0)$ decomposes into a linear combination of power series $\hat{Z}(q)$, which converges in $|q|<1$ and itself is an invariant of $Y$. Specifically, $$WRT[Y;k]= \frac{1}{i\sqrt{2k}} \sum_{a,b \in Spin^c (Y)} c^{WRT}_{ab}\, \hat{Z}_{b}(q) \Big\vert_{q \rightarrow e^{\frac{i2\pi}{k}}},$$ where $$\hat{Z}_{b}(Y;q) \in \frac{1}{2^c}q^{\Delta_{b}} \mathbb{Z}[[q]], \qquad |q|<1,\qquad \Delta_{b} \in \mathbb{Q},\quad c \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}.$$ Performing a Dehn surgery on a complement of a knot $
